segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, וְנָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ שׁוֹר אוֹ חֲמוֹר – חַיָּיב. אֶחָד הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר, שִׁיחַ וּמְעָרָה, חֲרִיצִין וּנְעִיצִין – חַיָּיב. אִם כֵּן לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר ״בּוֹר״? מָה בּוֹר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית – עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים; אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית – עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים. הָיוּ פְּחוּתִין מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, וְנָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ שׁוֹר אוֹ חֲמוֹר, וּמֵת – פָּטוּר. וְאִם הוּזַּק בּוֹ – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who digs a pit in the public domain and an ox or a donkey fell into it,» he is «liable.» The halakha is the «same» for «one who digs» either «a pit; a ditch,» which is narrow and long; «or a cave,» which is rectangular and roofed; «trenches and» water «channels.» In all these cases he is «liable. If so, why is» the verse «stated» as referring to «a pit,» as it states: “And if a man shall open a pit” (Exodus 21:33)? To teach that «just as a pit that has sufficient» depth «to cause death» when falling into it is at least «ten handbreadths» deep, «so too, any» other excavations «that have sufficient» depth «to cause death» may be no less than «ten handbreadths.» If any of the types of excavations «were less than ten handbreadths» deep, «and an ox or a donkey fell into» one of «them and died,» the digger of the excavation is «exempt. But if it was injured in it,» not killed, he is «liable» to pay damages.

moves.summary: digger of a pit, ditch, cave, trenches or channels is liable
the word 'pit' sets the lethal measure at ten handbreadths
moves.about: why the verse says 'pit': any excavation deep enough to kill (ten handbreadths) is included

moves.summary: under ten: exempt for death, liable for injury

edges.about: why the verse says 'pit': any excavation deep enough to kill (ten handbreadths) is included

positions.claim: any excavation of ten handbreadths renders the digger liable for death; less than ten, liable for injury only
